package.name: StrongholdProof
package.doc: One app, built once with current tools, and thin hosts that load it into a page the same way. The names follow the code: app/, hosts/server, hosts/online, hosts/dev.

elements.name: Page
elements.doc: A page with Stronghold on it: a SharePoint Server page, a SharePoint Online page, a Teams tab, or the dev page. Every Stronghold web part on the page mounts the same app, because the first entry file to load wins (app/src/host/load-app.ts).

elements.name: Host
elements.doc: hosts/: the small piece of code that plugs the app into one place. It works out where its package's files are, loads the entry file with the shared loader, and calls mount. It has no settings: it only ever loads the app from its own package.

elements.name: App
elements.doc: app/: Stronghold itself, built once with webpack 5 and TypeScript 5.9. Nothing in it knows about SharePoint.

elements.name: StrongholdApp
elements.doc: What the app's entry file registers on window.Stronghold.

elements.name: ServerHost
elements.doc: hosts/server: the web part for SharePoint Server.

elements.name: OnlineHost
elements.doc: hosts/online: the web part for SharePoint Online, which is also the Teams tab.

elements.name: DevHost
elements.doc: hosts/dev: a plain page that mounts the app the way the SharePoint hosts do. It never ships.

notes.text: Should Host stay abstract now that DevHost, the one host that never ships, is a part def of its own?
Is the mount one connection or one per host?
notes.response: One connection usage: hosts is [1..*], so each host's api is connected to the app's api.

notes.text: HostFiles, the package of files a host serves, is not drawn yet. Where does it go: beside Host, or inside it?

archive.response: No: Page is the SharePoint page itself, whichever host put the app on it, so the name stands.
archive.resolution: No: Page is the SharePoint page itself, whichever host put the app on it, so the name stands.
